<reflection>
The third experiment with low substrate (0.5 M) and low catalyst (0.01 M) further refined the NLL values, with M3 remaining the best fit. However, many mechanisms (e.g., M20, M9, M11, M14) are still within a narrow NLL range, indicating persistent uncertainty. The aim was to probe substrate dependence and deactivation effects; it succeeded in slightly separating some mechanisms but did not provide decisive discrimination across the entire set. New experimental conditions are needed to reduce uncertainty over all plausible candidates.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I propose introducing initial product to probe product-related effects, which have not been explored in previous experiments. By adding product at the start, mechanisms with reversible product steps (e.g., M1, M2) will show reduced net forward rates due to equilibrium shift. Mechanisms with product-induced deactivation (e.g., M12, M17) may exhibit faster deactivation, while those without product dependence (e.g., M9, M14) should be less affected. This experiment uses moderate substrate (1.0 M) and catalyst (0.02 M) to avoid saturation, with product at 0.2 M to ensure measurable effects. This design explores a new dimension (initial product concentration) and should provide orthogonal information to previous substrate and catalyst variations, helping to distinguish between multiple mechanism classes simultaneously.
</hypothesis>
